svg.title: How lead-send sends each e-mail once
svg.desc: How lead-send sends each e-mail once. Step 1, Freeze the e-mail (lead-approve): Approval freezes exactly what will be sent. If the resume file changes afterwards, the send is refused. Step 2, Reserve the attempt (lead-send): The attempt is recorded before the provider call, so a crash cannot lead to a second send. Step 3, Send (Gmail API): Accepted: the draft is marked sent and the attempt keeps the Gmail thread ID. Rejected: the attempt is marked failed with the reason; the draft stays ready but its approval is spent. Step 4, Response lost (timeout): A timeout or dropped connection marks the attempt unknown, not failed. Step 5, Never resent (lead-send (next run)): Running lead-send again cannot send a duplicate: an unknown attempt is never retried. Step 6, Settle from Sent (lead-reconcile): If the e-mail is in your Sent folder with the same action ID, it is marked sent. If not, it stays unknown, and lead-send refuses every other e-mail (unresolved_unknown) until it is settled.

text.font-family: Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
